title: Event-driven continuous-batcher and lease harmonizer
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
The continuous batching layer currently relies on a polling-driven commit cycle and a tight lease model that causes jitter under contention. Leases are aggressively reaped by the slot coordinator which leads to thrash (frequent slot reassignments) and repeated KV cache lookups. This ticket introduces an event-driven handoff for the batcher and a "lease harmonizer" that implements soft leases, heartbeat smoothing, and opportunistic redispatch to reduce churn and KV pressure.

Problem statement:
- High tail latency observed when load patterns oscillate; traced to repeated slot preemption and cache misses.
- KV-store read amplification during rapid handoffs increases latency and cost.
- Current scheduler polling frequency is a blunt instrument: decreasing poll intervals reduces latency but costs CPU; increasing them increases tail.

Goals:
1) Replace polling-heavy handoff with event-driven notifications from the slot-allocator to the batcher runtime for most common cases.
2) Implement a lease harmonizer that:
   - Introduces a soft-lease extension window (configurable ms) to avoid premature eviction under transient backpressure;
   - Adds heartbeat smoothing to avoid short-lived spikes triggering redispatch;
   - Performs opportunistic coalesced redispatch when reassignments are necessary to amortize KV reads.
3) Reduce KV read rate by >=35% in integration workloads and reduce 95th percentile latency by >=10% under oscillating load.

Out-of-scope:
- Rewriting the entire KV layer; this is a runtime/scheduler-focused refactor.
- Persistent store schema changes.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design and API:
   - Define event envelope between allocator and batcher (slot-grant, slot-revoke, soft-extend, queue-drain). Keep payloads small; use existing pubsub channel where possible.
   - Lease harmonizer config: soft_window_ms, heartbeat_alpha, coalesce_window_ms, max_coalesce_batch.

2) Prototype event-driven handoff (Spike, 3d):
   - Implement minimal event producer in slot-allocator (emit slot-grant/revoke).
   - Add event consumer in batcher that fast-paths event handoffs and falls back to poll on missing events.
   - Measure correctness and add metrics (events emitted, fallback polling counts).

3) Implement lease harmonizer (5d):
   - Soft-lease extension: add state machine to treat leases as extendable if no conflicting claims observed for soft_window.
   - Heartbeat smoothing: exponentially weighted moving average of slot load to filter microbursts.
   - Opportunistic coalesced redispatch: when multiple leases are revoked in coalesce_window, perform a single KV prefetch for affected keys.

4) Integration & load testing (4d):
   - Run synthetic oscillating workloads (sine wave and step patterns) across dedicated cluster and private infra.
   - Gather metrics: KV read/sec, slot reassign/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU cost of scheduler.

5) Rollout strategy:
   - Canary on 5% of traffic with runtime-1.24 flag enabled.
   - Monitor key signals for 24h: error rate, KV ops, tail latency.
   - Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with automated rollback on safety gates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for event consumers/producers and lease state machine.
- KV read/sec reduced by >=35% in benchmark harness and slot reassign/sec reduced by >=40% in same tests.
- 95th percentile latency down >=10% on oscillating load.
- No increase in error rate or mission-critical SLO violations during canary phase.

Backward compatibility and fallback:
- Event-driven handoff is additive; if allocator fails to emit events the batcher auto-falls back to polling mode (configurable poll interval).
- Soft-lease parameters are runtime-configurable and can be disabled cluster-wide.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: missed events could cause stall — mitigation: always keep a heartbeat/lease TTL and conservative fallback timers.
- Risk: coalesced prefetches pull more keys than necessary and spike memory — mitigation: cap max_coalesce_batch and monitor memory.
- Risk: mis-tuned soft_window may increase latency under high contention — mitigation: expose canary-grade telemetry and a/b toggle.

Observability additions:
- New metrics: slot_event_emitted, slot_event_consumed, fallback_poll_count, soft_lease_extensions, coalesced_prefetch_count, kv_reads_saved.
- Dashboards: event handoff success rate, harmonizer health, per-node downstream KV ops.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on correctness of lease state transitions and ensuring we never violate exclusive-use assumptions for hot slots.
- The event envelope intentionally avoids embedding full KV keys to keep event small; coalesced prefetch will fetch keys after an initial notification.

Documentation:
- Update runtime-ops runbook with toggles and rollback steps.
- Add a short design doc in Drive: Drive:/Redwood/runtime/harmonizer-design-2026 (link in comments).
